title: must and can't
subtitle: You must be tired / You can't be hungry
summary: Use must when you believe something is certain and can't when you believe it is not possible, in the present (must be) and in the past (must have been).

lesson.heading: must = we believe it is certain
lesson.text: Imagine somebody tells you: *My house is very near the motorway.* You can answer: *It **must be** very noisy.* We use **must** to say that we believe something is certain.

examples.text: You've been travelling all day. You **must be** tired.
examples.note: travelling is tiring and you've been travelling all day, so you must be tired

examples.text: 'Joe is a hard worker.' 'Joe? You **must be joking**. He doesn't do anything.'
Louise **must get** very bored in her job. She does the same thing every day.

lesson.heading: can't = we believe it is not possible
lesson.text: We use **can't** to say that we believe something is not possible.

examples.text: You've just had lunch. You **can't be** hungry already.
examples.note: we don't expect people to be hungry immediately after a meal

examples.text: They haven't lived here for very long. They **can't know** many people.

lesson.heading: The past: must have and can't have
lesson.text: Martin and Lucy expected their friends to be at home. They rang the doorbell twice, but nobody has answered. Lucy says: *They **must have gone** out.* (= there is no other possibility). For the past we use **must have ...** and **can't have ...**.

examples.text: I lost one of my gloves. I **must have dropped** it somewhere.
examples.note: that's the only explanation I can think of

examples.text: 'We used to live very near the motorway.' 'Did you? It **must have been** noisy.'
Sarah hasn't contacted me. She **can't have got** my message.
Max walked into a wall. He **can't have been looking** where he was going.

lesson.heading: The structure: must / can't have + ...
rows: He **can't have been looking** where he was going.

lesson.heading: couldn't have = can't have
lesson.text: You can use **couldn't have** instead of can't have. The meaning is the same.

examples.text: Max **couldn't have been looking** where he was going.

lesson.text: must = 'I'm sure it is'; can't = 'I'm sure it isn't'. For the past, add have: must have been / can't have been.

exercises.prompt: That restaurant ___ be very good. It's always full of people.
exercises.explanation: A full restaurant makes us sure it is good: must = we believe it is certain.

exercises.prompt: That restaurant ___ be very good. It's always empty.
exercises.explanation: An empty restaurant makes us believe it is not possible that it is good: can't.

exercises.prompt: Which word completes each sentence: must or can't?

items.text: I'm sure Kate gave me her address. I ___ have it somewhere.
I often see that man in this street. He ___ live near here.
It rained every day during their holiday. It ___ have been very nice for them.
Congratulations on passing your exam. You ___ be very pleased.
This bill ___ be correct. It's much too high.
Bill and Sue always stay at five-star hotels. They ___ be short of money.
Karen hasn't left the office yet. She ___ be working late tonight.

exercises.prompt: 'How old is Ed?' 'He's older than me. He ___ at least 40.'
I don't seem to have my wallet with me. I ___ it at home.
exercises.explanation: The only explanation for something in the past: must have + past participle.

exercises.prompt: 'You're going on holiday soon. You ___ forward to it.' 'Yes, I am.'
exercises.explanation: Something happening now that we are sure about: must be + -ing.

exercises.prompt: I didn't hear my phone. I ___ asleep.
exercises.explanation: A past state we are sure about: must have been asleep.

exercises.prompt: 'Do you have a car?' 'You ___! How could I afford to have a car?'
exercises.explanation: The speaker is sure the other person is joking now: must be joking.

exercises.prompt: The jacket you bought is very good quality. Make a sentence with must have about its price.
exercises.answer: It must have been very expensive.
exercises.explanation: A conclusion about the past: must have been.

exercises.prompt: There was a man standing outside the cafe. He was there a long time. Make a sentence with must have about why he was there.
exercises.answer: He must have been waiting for somebody.
exercises.explanation: An action in progress in the past: must have been + -ing.

exercises.statement: Rachel did the opposite of what I asked her to do. She must have understood what I said.
exercises.explanation: She can't have understood what I said (or She couldn't have understood ...). We believe it is not possible that she understood.

exercises.statement: Paul has had these shoes for years, but they still look new. He can't have worn them much.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Can't have + past participle = we believe this was not possible in the past.

exercises.prompt: The light was red, but the car didn't stop. The driver ___ the red light.
exercises.explanation: We are sure the driver did not see the light. Past + not possible = can't have seen (or couldn't have seen).
